A backreference refers back to a captured group in the same regex, using `\1`, `\2`, etc. for the 1st, 2nd, captured groups. Example: `(\w+)\s+\1` matches repeated words separated by whitespace. ``` "hello hello" → matches (captures "hello" in group 1, `\1` matches it again) "hello world" → no match ``` Practical use: `<(\w+)>.*?` matches paired HTML tags like `
content
` but rejects mismatched pairs like `
content`.
